body.content: Speculative: the 1/9 lost mutation might be the same class as the AU-4 erratum — a closed-negative literal that cannot name the generated `discharged(c)`. If compile.py's mutation operator generated such a literal, the test would fail to parse, and the failure would be recorded as a lost mutation rather than a test failure. This would mean the test was never given the chance to constrain the subject.
body.possible_next_move: Check whether the 1/9 mutation in the record is a closed-negative literal or a parse-time failure.
body.why_keep_this: Links the AU-4 erratum to the mutation-testing asymmetry.
